technical-data.invention-title: PREFABRICATED MODULAR STATIONS FOR WASHING AND SERVICING MOTOR VEHICLES
STATIONS MODULAIRES PREFABRIQUEES DE LAVAGE ET D'ENTRETIEN POUR VEHICULES AUTOMOBILES

nplcit.text: PATENT ABSTRACTS OF JAPAN vol. 015, no. 267 (M-1133), 8 July 1991 (1991-07-08) & JP 03 090455 A (KOICHI NISHIKAWA;OTHERS: 01), 16 April 1991 (1991-04-16)

abstract.p: Prefabricated modular stations, intended for washing and providing various services for motor vehicles, consisting of a technological or service module (12) having, arranged alongside it, one platform (22) for washing or various services possibly covered by roof structures (14) or awning-type tensile structures (42, 62), the at least one washing platform (22) being able to contain tanks for initial treatment of water used during washing. As a result of the modular nature of the parts of the stations, it is possible to construct a large variety of said stations using a small number of components. A method for transporting and assembling these modular stations at the installation site is also described.

L'invention concerne des stations préfabriquées modulaires destinées au lavage et à la fourniture de services divers pour véhicules automobiles, comprenant un module technologique ou de service (12) le long duquel est agencée une plate-forme (22) de lavage ou de services divers pouvant être recouverte par des structures de toit (14) ou des structures tendues (42, 62) de type tente, la plate-forme de lavage (22) au moins pouvant contenir des réservoirs destinés au traitement initial de l'eau utilisée pendant le lavage. Du fait de la nature modulaire des parties constituant les stations, il est possible de construire une grande variété desdites stations à l'aide d'un petit nombre de constituants. Un procédé de transport et d'assemblage de ces stations modulaires sur le site d'installation est également décrit.

description.p: PREFABRICATED MODULAR STAΗONS FOR WASHING AND SERVICING MOTOR VEHICLES

The present invention, which is an improvement to the invention covered by the Italian Patent No. 01256147 entitled "Self-sufficient station for washing motor vehicles, composed of one or more transportable units", filed on 17 September 1992 in the name of Swiss Wash S.r.l., belonging to the proprietor of the present application, relates to prefabricated modular stations for washing and providing various services for motor vehicles, which may be constructed with a large variety of 0 dimensions depending on the availability of space in the location where they are to be built and the requirements of the users who are to be served, and to a method for transportation and assembly thereof at the installation site.

At present, it is extremely advantageous to be able to construct stations for washing motor vehicles using a minimum number of modular components which 5 may be reproduced as far as possible, whereby said elements must also have dimensions such as to allow transportation by road on standard-size vehicles, thus avoiding all the problems associated with the transportation of exceptional loads.

As already stated in the abovementioned Italian patent, it is known that a washing station for motor vehicles, if constructed in a traditional manner by means of 0 building works and fixed installations, risks becoming unusable if, for any reason, traffic were no longer to pass through the area where it is constructed. It is also known that, should it become unusable, it would be extremely difficult to disassemble, transport and reassemble a washing plant in a new location and sometimes its cost could exceed that of building a brand new plant and moreover all 5 the buildings would be put to no use, having to be abandoned or, even worse, demolished.
It is also known that, with every building structure, it is always advantageous if there is the need for a smallest possible variety of components because the problems associated with adaptation of said components are reduced and the costs of warehouse storage are also reduced. The reduction in the number of components is greatly helped by standardisation of said components which makes them suitable for construction of the largest possible part of a plant.

The solution to the problems associated with the modular design and reduction in number of the components necessary for prefabricated modular stations intended for washing and providing various services for motor vehicles is provided by the present invention which comprises a technological or service module having, arranged alongside it, at least one platform for washing or various services, characterized in that the at least one washing platform consists of modular elements in the form of parallelepipeds, the lengthwise and widthwise dimensions of which are chosen so that at least one pair of them may be loaded on a normal road-transport trailer and the heightwise dimension of which is chosen so as to allow a vehicle to drive up easily onto the said platform from the ground level.

Preferably, in modular stations, the modular elements of the washing platforms have lengthwise dimensions of 6 metres, widthwise dimensions of 2.5 metres and heightwise dimensions of not greater than 50 cm. Even more preferably, the modular elements have heightwise dimensions of
45 cm.
In particular, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module without a housing and by an uncovered platform.
Alternatively, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module provided with a housing and by an uncovered platform.

By way of a further alternative, the prefabricated modular stations are
characterized by a technological module without a housing and by a covered platform having, arranged above them, a roof structure supported by uprights.

By way of a further alternative, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module provided with a housing and by a covered platform having, arranged above them, a roof structure supported by uprights.
By way of yet another alternative, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module without a housing, by a first uncovered platform and by a second uncovered platform.
Also by way of alternative, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module provided with a housing, by a first uncovered platform and by a second uncovered platform.

According to other solutions, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module without housing, by a first covered platform and by a second covered platform having, arranged above them, a roof structure supported by uprights.

In addition, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module provided with a housing, by a first covered platform and by a second covered platform having, arranged above them, a roof structure supported by uprights. Alternatively, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module provided with a housing, by a first covered platform, by a second covered platform having, arranged above them, a roof structure supported by uprights and by a first uncovered platform.

By way of a further alternative, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module provided with a housing, by a first covered platform, by a second covered platform having, arranged above them, a roof structure
supported by uprights, by a first uncovered platform and by a second uncovered platform.

By way of a further alternative, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module provided with a housing, by a first covered platform, by a second covered platform, by a third covered platform and by a fourth covered platform having, arranged above them, a roof structure supported by uprights.

Also by way of an alternative, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module provided with a housing, by a first covered platform, by a second covered platform, by a third covered platform, by a fourth covered platform having, arranged above them, a roof structure supported by uprights, by a first uncovered platform and by a second uncovered platform.

By way of a further alternative, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a technological module provided with a housing, by a first covered platfoπΗ, by a second covered platform, by a third covered platform, by a fourth covered platform, by a fifth covered platform and by a sixth covered platform having, arranged above them, a roof structure supported by uprights.

Furthermore, prefabricated modular stations, especially designed for the washing of industrial vehicles, are characterized by a technological module, without a housing, and by a reinforced uncovered platform able to support industrial vehicles, the platform being provided with an automatic washing plant of the rotating brush or roller type.

Moreover, prefabricated modular stations designed for the washing both of industrial vehicles and motor cars are characterized by a technological module without a housing, by a first reinforced uncovered platform for the washing of industrial vehicles and by several uncovered platforms for the washing of cars and
vans, where the first reinforced platform is provided with an automatic washing plant.

In addition, the prefabricated modular stations for tyre and minor mechanical repair services are characterized by a room for spare part storage and administration and by a platform provided with a lifting deck.

Also in addition, the prefabricated modular stations for tyre and repair workshop services are characterized by a room for spare part storage and administration, by a first covered platform provided with a lifting deck for the tyre service, by a second covered platform provided with a lifting deck for the repair workshop service and by an uncovered platform provided with a lifting deck for the open-air mechanical workshop service, the spare parts storage and administration room and the two covered platforms having, arranged above them, a roof structure supported by uprights.

By way of a further addition, the prefabricated modular stations are characterized by a mini-market service on a first platform, an automatic washing service of the roller type on a second platform, a first manual washing service, of the self-service type, on a third platform, a technological module, a second manual washing service, of the self-service type, on a fourth platform, a tyre service on a fifth platform, a spare part storage and administration room and a repair workshop service on a sixth platform, the whole station having, arranged above it, a roof structure supported by uprights.

Again according to the present invention, a method for transporting prefabricated modular stations is provided, characterized by production and storage of platform elements, by loading the platform elements onto a first semi-trailer provided with an independent crane, by hitching-up a driving cab to the semi-trailer so as to start consignment, and further characterized by production and the storage of
at least one technological or service module and structural elements, by loading the technological or service module and the structural elements onto a second semitrailer provided with an independent crane and by hitching-up a driving cab to the semi-trailer so as to start consignment. In addition, the method for installing prefabricated modular stations is characterized by constructing, on a concourse, a station supplying fuel or the like and a levelled asphalt covering layer and by placing, on the said asphalt covering layer, the platfomi elements supplied from the first semi-trailer and the technological or service module and the structural elements supplied from the second semi-trailer. Alternatively, the method for installing prefabricated modular stations is characterized by constructing, on a concourse, a station supplying fuel or the like and a levelled reinforced-concrete flooring, after carrying out an excavation for receiving the said flooring, and by placing, on the said flooring, the platform elements supplied from the first semi-trailer and the technological or service module and the structural elements supplied from the second semi-trailer.

Considering Figure 1 firstly, it can be seen that a modular washing station 10 according to the invention consists of a plant 12 for prepanng and treating water and washing products, or technological module, a roof structure 14, consisting of an assembly of beams 16 supported by uprights or columns 18 and 20, and platforms 22, 24 and 26 having the function of receiving vehicles such as a car 28, an all-terrain vehicle 30 or a lorry 32. The assembly of beams 16 has, suspended underneath it, articulated arms 34a-h which are designed to carry cleaning equipment, such as guns
supplying water and detergents and suction pipes for vacuum-cleaning functions.

The platforms 22, 24 and 26 supporting the vehicles 28, 30 and 32 may be, or rather are preferably, of the type forming bays containing tanks for storing water and sludge and for treating washing water, as described and claimed in Italian Patent Application No. MI98A002481, entitled "Tanks for treating water used for washing motor vehicles, to be installed underneath bays in centres for washing said motor vehicles", filed on 17 November 1998 in the name of the proprietor of the present application, to which reference should be made for an understanding of the detailed aspects. By way of example, Figure 1A shows schematically a prospective view of a modular platfoπn element 22a in the form of a parallelepiped-shaped structural tank, the dimensions of which are standard and have been carefully chosen so as to allow the transportation, on standard vehicles, of the largest possible number of parts. For example, a modular element 22a which is very advantageous from an applicational point of view has an edge 25 which is 6 metres long, an edge 27 which is 2.5 metres wide and an edge 29 which is 45 cm high, these dimensions being suitable for the loading of a number of elements 22a, ranging between four and six, onto a semitrailer, thus making particularly easy the transportation of the platform elements for the construction of stations according to the invention. Examining Figure 23 it is possible to see a second refuelling station 60 containing, among other things, also a unit 62 for washing and any miscellaneous services for motor vehicles, formed by a technological module 12 and by eight platforms 22,, 222, 223, 224, 24,, 24,, 243 and 244, covered by an awning 64 of the type known as a "tensile structure". Figures 24 to 29 illustrate a method for the transportation, from the production site to the installation site, of platforms such as the platforms 22 illustrated in Figures 1 to 14. As can be seen in Figure 24, platform elements 22,,

222, 22λ, 224, etc. are prepared and kept stored in a production plant 70. As can be seen in Figure 25, the platform elements 22, - 224 are loaded onto a first semi-trailer 72 provided with an independent crane 74, ensuring that these platform elements are loaded in a direction such that they remain within the overall dimensional limits of semi-trailers for ordinary transportation which do not require special authorisation for the transportation of exceptional loads. In fact the platform elements 22, - 224 are constructed with their smaller side having a length less than or equal to the standard width of the semi-trailer 72. The dimensions of these elements have been mentioned in connection with the description of Figure 1A. As can be seen in Figure 26, once the platform elements have been loaded and suitably fixed onto the semi-trailer 72, a driving cab 76 is hitched up to the semi-trailer so that the platforms are ready for consignment.

As can be seen in Figure 27, in addition to the platforms 22, - 224, at least one technological module 12 and all the structural elements 78 of a washing station according to the invention are prepared and kept stored in the same production plant

70. As can be seen in Figure 28, the technological module 12 and the structural elements 78 are hoisted onto a second semi-trailer 80 by means of its independent crane 82 and, as can be seen in Figure 29, once the load has been arranged in position and fixed onto the second semi-trailer 80, a driving cab 84 is hitched up to the semi- trailer 80 so that the structural elements 78 are ready for consignment.

Figures 30 to 34 show a method for installing a washing station according to
the invention. As can be seen in Figure 30, on a concourse 90 of a station supplying fuel or the like, it is possible to cast a simple covering layer 92 of asphalt 92 which is levelled, i.e. made perfectly flat and kept horizontal or with a desired inclination in order to favour the flow-off of liquids. As can be seen in Figures 31 and 32, a mechanical shovel excavator 94 performs an excavation 96 of limited depth (less than 50 cm) in a concourse 90 of a station supplying fuel or the like and a levelled flooring 98 of reinforced concrete is cast into the said excavation 96. Then, as can be seen in Figure 33, a semi-trailer 72 unloads, by means of its independent crane 74, the platfonn elements 22,, 222, 223, etc., placing them on the flooring 98. Finally, as can be seen in Figure 34, a semi-trailer 80 unloads, by means of its own crane 82, the technological module 12 and the remainder of the structural elements 78 so as to form a washing station according to the invention.

The above description describes several examples of prefabricated washing stations constructed with elements which are repetitive and modular so as to reduce to a minimum the number of components to be kept in store and which have dimensions chosen so as to allow transportation on standard vehicles, avoiding all the problems associated with the transportation of exceptional loads. These examples are not to be regarded as limiting the scope of the invention which will be defined only by the claims which are appended below. For example, the washing station for industrial vehicles, shown in Figure 15, may be adapted for the washing of industrial vehicles other than lorries, such as trams or railway carriages and wagons, it being sufficient in this case to provide the platfonn 26p with rails for said carriages or wagons to travel along. Again for carriages travelling on rails it is possible to envisage a plurality of uncovered platfonns 26p also provided with rails, so as to allow the simultaneous washing of a plurality of said carriages.
